tagline: A thoughtful notebook, rooted in observation and everyday humanity.
typography: Georgia for literary warmth; Arial for specimen labels and readable information.
rationale: Original botanical line art, specimen labels and field-note structure reinterpret nature through an editorial system rather than generic forest imagery.
mobile: Illustration follows the hero copy; numbered sections retain orientation; notebook labels wrap cleanly.
supporting: Biography, actual methods and practical logistics form a clear anchored guide; FAQs expand in place.
trust: Process language is qualified and placeholders require confirmation; practical details are easy to reach without sharing personal information.
seo: Meaningful local and service information is live text; artwork is lightweight. Botanical metaphors should accompany literal service labels, not replace them.
tradeoff: Nature motifs are common in this category; differentiation depends on disciplined typography and original illustration.
name: The Field Guide
accessibility: Notebook labels should remain large enough to read. Botanical art is decorative. Native details controls preserve keyboard access to practical information without adding bespoke interactions.
